title: HiLight: A Comprehensive Framework for High-Performance and Lightweight Scalability in Surface Code Communication
problem: Intersecting braiding paths in surface code quantum error correction create communication bottlenecks that increase circuit latency. The double-defect mode enables long-range two-qubit communication but suffers from performance degradation when multiple braiding operations intersect.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires efficient quantum error correction protocols with minimal communication overhead to achieve practical, scalable quantum processors.
method: HiLight optimizes surface code communication by reducing path intersections through routing and scheduling techniques. The framework employs layout-aware compilation and braiding operation scheduling to minimize latency in quantum circuits while maintaining lightweight implementation.
key_novelty: A comprehensive framework for eliminating surface code communication bottlenecks from intersecting braiding paths through intelligent routing and scheduling without sacrificing scalability.
contributions: Identification of communication bottlenecks in surface code braiding-based two-qubit operations
HiLight framework design for high-performance lightweight quantum error correction
Optimization techniques for braiding path scheduling to reduce circuit latency
Demonstration of improved scalability for fault-tolerant quantum computing
limitations: Not discussed in the provided abstract; specific quantitative comparisons and baseline systems are not detailed.
primary_theme: optimizing surface code communication for scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing
